nodes.long_description:
VR Link Player turns any video link, or your own files, into your private cinema.

PLAY WHAT YOU LINK
• Movies and shows in 2D or 3D, 180° and 360° video, pictures and playlists.
• Links, live streams, your headset's files, home servers and Windows or NAS shares.
• A cinema-sized screen to stretch with a grab, or curve around you.
• The right mode is picked for you; opens from web pages and apps.

2D MADE 3D, TRUE COLORS
• Any flat video or photo in real 3D: each frame its own depth, made on your headset, even 8K at 60 fps.
• Accurate colors: SDR as made for TV, HDR tone-mapped to each scene.

SMOOTH ON HUGE FILES
• Downloads ahead as you watch: seeking back is instant, even if the connection drops.
• See the frames as you drag the seek bar; jump ±10s with the thumbstick.
• Picks up where you left off, with your audio and subtitles.

SUBTITLES IN YOUR LANGUAGE
• The video's own tracks, or OpenSubtitles with your free account.
• AI translates subtitles into 80 languages, or makes them from the audio, with your free Groq key.
• Place them where you like, even over 3D; nudge their timing.

MADE FOR COMFORT
• The room around you starts pitch black; brighten it any time.
• Speed from 0.25× to 2×, snap turn, recenter for watching lying down.
• Controller buttons play, pause and stop; a built-in guide shows them all.
• Details at a glance: resolution, HDR, codecs, every track.

You bring the links: VR Link Player doesn't provide or find video.
nodes.short_description: Paste a link or pick a file, press play: your videos on a giant screen or all around you in 180°/360°, with subtitles in your language.

nodes.long_description:
VR Link Player plays video from a direct web link, on a big flat screen or all around you.

- Flat 2D on a cinema-sized screen in the video's own shape, or 180° and 360° video, mono or 3D (side-by-side, top/bottom). The right mode is picked from the video itself.
- Smooth on long, high-bitrate files: the video is kept on the headset as it downloads, so seeking  back is instant and a dropped connection doesn't stop what's already there.
- Pictures and playlists too, stepped through with A and B.
- Subtitles in your language and English: the video's own tracks; OpenSubtitles with your free API key and account; or AI subtitles made from the audio, with your own free Groq API key.
- Grab the subtitles to move them where they're comfortable to read, even over 3D.
- Snap turn, ±10 s seeks on the thumbstick, recenter with the Meta button.

You supply the links: VR Link Player doesn't provide or find video. Subtitle services are optional and use your own accounts.
nodes.short_description: Play videos from any web link on a cinema screen or in 180°/360° — with subtitles in your language and English.

nodes.change_log:
Steadier 3D depth
• 3D's depth is now found from every pixel of a video up to 4K, not a few of them, so it flickers about 13% less. Above 4K, as 8K, from a 16th of them, 10% less flicker for the cost of a 4K frame.
• 8K60 and 4K60 with 3D, accurate colors and AI subtitles play as evenly as before.
• The app's log now notes each time the headset recenters, by you or by itself when put on, to help find problems.

A background image, shares found for you, and voice typing
• New: a background image. Turn it on beside the room's brightness, and with the room black a 180° scene shows around a flat or curved screen, a picture or the link panel. There are 10 scenes in a random order, changing every 3 minutes (1 to 60 in Settings' new Image tab), with ↻ whenever you like, or only with ↻ using the clock button. Each downloads the first time it's shown, and Storage clears them. Off by default, and not available for 180° or 360° video, which covers it.
• It uses the GPU while it shows: 4K60 with 3D, accurate colors and AI subtitles stays even, with a few more uneven frames (about 0.4%). 8K with all of that on a large screen gets hot enough to slow down, with about 4 to 8% of frames uneven, against about 1.5% without it. Once it's hidden, its memory is freed.
• Files' Network tab now lists the Windows and NAS shares on your network by itself, and a server's own link lists its shares, asking for a login if it needs one.
• Voice typing: the keyboard's mic now shows for movie and show searches, user names and domains, as well as feedback. Links keep the keyboard with / and .com, and passwords and keys have no mic.
• The keyboard's Submit key now plays a link, opens a folder link or searches for a title, as those buttons do.
• Settings' Keep tab always shows its Back button, and the room's controls are the same on the link panel and in a video's settings.
• Subtitle keys are checked once when their tab first shows, and again only after an edit or Check again.

Steadier playback through everything you change
• Each frame is shown at the refresh it's meant for, from the very first frame: 4K60 with 3D, accurate colors and AI subtitles on holds an even pace, about one frame off in a minute; uneven frames in 8K60 are down to about 0.5%.
• No more freezes of up to 0.8 s in 8K HDR's most colorful scenes, when turning 3D on, or stutter after resizing the screen.
• A video opened from the app no longer skips its first frames, and picture and sound line up within about a refresh from the first frame.
• Turning accurate colors or 3D on or off, curving the screen, resizing it and switching between flat, 180° and 360° no longer freeze: the picture plays on through them. Curving or flattening the screen is now instant.
• Speeds: 1.25× and 1.5× now show every frame of 60 fps video up to 4K, 3D included; 2× shows about 100 frames a second in 3D, all but a few without it. Changing speed no longer stalls the picture.
• Pictures can be curved like the video's screen.
• Video is drawn at the size that keeps it sharpest for what the GPU can take: on a large screen in 3D, 8K at 24 or 30 fps is drawn far larger than before. 8K without 3D uses up to 20% less of the GPU at large sizes. The flat screen's usual size is a little larger, so 4K and 8K are drawn exactly to fit, and resizing settles on those exact sizes when you let go near them.
• The controllers, hands and pointer look clearer: the app's own eye buffer is now 1024 × 1024.
• Fixed: if the headset's sound stops after many hours on, the app now restarts it and the video plays on, instead of staying frozen until a restart.

Smoother playback, sharper 3D, and control over what's kept
• Settings: choose how much the app keeps on the headset — History, playback positions, subtitles, cached videos and pictures (by number or by size: 100 GB and 10 GB by default) and video indexes. A changed setting is marked with ↺ and applies when Settings closes.
• Keep: the download icon next to a file's name keeps what's downloaded of it, whatever the limits; kept files are listed in History's new Kept tab. Remove a single link from History with ×.
• Share: send a link, or a getlk.net page that opens it in the player.
• The controls show the date, time and battery. A name cut short shows in full when you point at it. Files reopens where you left it, with the folder you came from highlighted.
• The headset's refresh rate now matches the video's frame rate: 24 fps at 72 Hz, 25 and 50 fps at 100 Hz, 30 fps at 90 Hz, 48 fps at 96 Hz and 60 fps at 120 Hz, so every frame is shown for the same time.
• Each frame is shown at the refresh it's meant for: uneven frames in 8K60 down from 18% to 1%, and none in 4K60 or 1080p30.
• Picture and sound line up within about half a refresh from the first frame.
• 2× speed plays 60 fps video up to 4K at its full frame rate (it was held to about 74 frames a second).
• Turning 3D or accurate colors on or off, curving the screen and resizing it no longer flash black or make the video jump; turning 3D off no longer leaves the screen black for seconds.
• 3D starts faster: its depth model loads in 0.3 s instead of about 2.5 s.
• Sharper, steadier 3D: each eye of an 8K video is drawn at exactly half its size, the picture's left and right edges stay black instead of stretched, and HDR10 video is tone-mapped before its depth is found.
• The smallest screen size is now 55% of the usual, where even 8K video shows no flashing dark specks.
• Less GPU and memory: the app's own eye buffer is 512 × 512 (0.2 ms of the GPU a frame at 8K60 in 3D instead of 1.2, and 64 MB less), and 3D lets go of 66 MB when it's turned off.
• Fixed: the picture could freeze for good after brief stalls at the start of an 8K video; 8K AV1 video dropped frames.
• Downloads: a seek stops the old download at once (seeks start about 0.1 s sooner), the cache writes to storage in larger pieces, and reaching the storage limit no longer removes an extra older video.
• Dolby audio starts at once when you come back to the app (it took 1 to 2 s).

Back in the app after allowing files access
• Allowing all files access for the Files panel's Local tab now brings you straight back to the player, with the headset's videos and pictures listed, instead of leaving you in Home.
